newsitem.title: USA: Galileo reservation system sets $700 million deal.
newsitem.headline: Galileo reservation system sets $700 million deal.

text.p: Galileo International Partnership, an electronic travel services company owned by several airlines, said Tuesday it reached agreement with United Airlines and other carriers to buy marketing group Apollo Travel Services Partnerships for $700 million.
United holds a 77 percent stake in Apollo, which markets the Galileo services in the United States, Mexico, and the Caribbean. US Airways owns 21 percent and Air Canada 2 percent.

Galileo, which lets travel agencies access schedule and fare information, book reservations and issue tickets for 525 airlines, also said it filed an initial public offering plan with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Galileo said its current 11 airline owners will each retain an ownership interest in the company.
